title: LOV-REF-TABLE carries 25 table codes in v4 but the rwb-case reference-data contract fixes twelve
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reference Data and Lists of Values v4.xlsx; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P3 rwb-case (Case and workflow)/RWB P3 E1043 CON Reference data service with versioned tables - contract v1.md
section: Lists row LOV-REF-TABLE; Values rows LOV-REF-TABLE (25 codes); Reference data starter
description: The Lists sheet gives LOV-REF-TABLE as a closed list of 25 values (PRODUCT, REGION, EXPOSURE_BAND, ROLE, TEAM, QUEUE, QUEUE_MEMBER, SERVICE_LEVEL, DOCUMENT_TYPE, DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST, RETENTION_CLASS, TEMPLATE, DELEGATION_LIMIT, PERMISSION, MASKING_RULE, PARTNER_USER, LEGAL_PERIOD, HOLIDAY, PRODUCT_PARAMETER, PARAMETER, ENTRY, EXCLUSION, ALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT, TRANSFER). The D-RCV-60 contract story RWB-P3-E1043-CON states that LOV-REF-TABLE carries the twelve table codes of legacy section 8 BR1, eleven of them served by rwb-case and DELEGATION_LIMIT answered by the rwb-access DoA operation. The two counts differ, and so does the number of codes each list serves.
evidence: Lists row LOV-REF-TABLE ('Closed list', '25'); Values rows LOV-REF-TABLE code 1 to 25, all valid from 30 Nov 2026; RWB P3 E1043 CON section 3 ('The list LOV-REF-TABLE carries the twelve table codes of legacy section 8 BR1 and no rule table code') and section 7 AC1 ('the twelve LOV-REF-TABLE codes of legacy section 8 BR1 are listed, eleven of them are served here and DELEGATION_LIMIT is answered by the rwb-access DoA operation'); RWB-P3-E1043-CON section 12.7 names reference_row, reference_version and lov_value as the three tables of the surface.
area: Data / reference table codes and the reference-data contract
proposed: Copy the 25 values unchanged in v5 and let the contract name its twelve as a subset of the same list; the reference data administrator reconciles the two sets before the first approved reference load in wave 1, and no value is removed from this workbook in the realignment.

title: LOV-MATCH-TYPE is used by payment_match_rule, a table the target drops and the Ownership Map does not carry
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reference Data and Lists of Values v4.xlsx; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Architecture Decision Records v3.md (ADR-012); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
section: Lists row LOV-MATCH-TYPE; Values rows LOV-MATCH-TYPE (EXACT, WINDOW, PARTIAL); Reference data starter row P8
description: The Lists sheet gives the use of LOV-MATCH-TYPE as payment_match_rule.match_type. payment_match_rule is not one of the 93 tables of the Ownership Map, so no owning service and no schema can be read for it, and ADR-012 of the latest Architecture Decision Records drops the table: payment matching becomes package PAYMENT_MATCH with match type, tolerance, window, grace and partial floor as decision-table columns. The three codes are therefore a column of a rule package in rwb_decision, not a column of a table in a service schema.
evidence: Lists row LOV-MATCH-TYPE ('Closed list', '3', used by 'payment_match_rule.match_type'); Architecture Decision Records v3 ADR-012 decision bullet 'payment_match_rule is dropped. Payment matching is package PAYMENT_MATCH, with match type, tolerance, window, grace and partial floor as decision-table columns'; Ownership Map sheet Tables 93 rows with no payment_match_rule row; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (P7 rwb-decision owns the DMN model registry) and slide 44 (JOB-07 payment matching in rwb-payment).
area: Data / payment matching list and rule packages
proposed: Record P7 rwb-decision as the holder of the three codes and P8 rwb-payment as the reader, with the codes carried as the match type column of the PAYMENT_MATCH package and the package version recorded in the decision log; the value rows of the Values sheet are copied unchanged.

title: Two services derive no starter row: S1 rwb-valuation and S7 rwb-writeoff
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reference Data and Lists of Values v4.xlsx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
description: The starter takes a row from a list's 'Used by' cell and the owner of the table named there. No list names a table owned by S1 rwb-valuation (the map gives S1 no table row) and no list names write_off, the one S7 rwb-writeoff table, so both services appear in no starter row even though both evaluate lists: valuation reads product group, exposure band and stage, and write-off reads the product, closure and write-off codes. The starter is therefore complete for 17 services and the platform library and open for two.
evidence: Ownership Map sheet Tables: 93 rows, no row with owner S1, one row write_off with owner S7; Lists sheet 'Used by' cells name no write_off column and no rwb_valuation table; the Reference data starter sheet of v5 holds 179 rows over 18 codes: all ten P services, S2, S3, S4, S5, S6, S8 and S9, and the platform library.
area: Data / reference data starter per service
proposed: Name in each service story the lists it reads, and add the S1 and S7 rows at the next revision of this workbook; v5 records the two services as open rather than inventing a row for them.

title: No source states which lists a service needs at its first deployment
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reference Data and Lists of Values v4.xlsx; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1
description: The realignment needs a refdata starter: the set of lists and reference tables each of the 19 services must have at its first deployment. No source enumerates that set. The v4 workbook gives one list-to-column map (the 'Used by' column), the Ownership Map gives one owner and one wave per table and per service, and each service story names its own configuration in its section 13, but no document puts the three together. v5 derives the starter by rule from the first two and records the rule on the sheet.
evidence: v4 has no starter sheet: its five sheets are Lists, Values, Reference tables, Change process and Key; the Ownership Map sheet Services gives the wave of each service (19 rows) and sheet Tables the owner of each table (93 rows); the service stories of 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1 name configuration and reference data per story only.
proposed: Keep the derivation stated on the sheet (the service that owns a table whose column uses the list, or the ACE view the column is read from, or the reference table itself) and have each service story confirm its rows at its design review; a later revision replaces the derived rows with confirmed ones.

title: Four source lists are held in another service's table although the sheet calls every list Workbench-held
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reference Data and Lists of Values v4.xlsx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
section: Lists rows LOV-DECISION, LOV-DOC-TYPE, LOV-RETENTION and LOV-ROLE; Lists header note
description: The Lists header says every list is 'held and versioned in the Workbench', and 23 rows name the ACE view or the Workbench table their values come from. After the split the values of four of those lists live in four different schemas: rule_row in rwb_decision (LOV-DECISION, P7), document_type and retention_rule in rwb_document (LOV-DOC-TYPE and LOV-RETENTION, P5), and role in rwb_access (LOV-ROLE, P4). The rwb-case list read serves lov_value, reference_row and reference_version only, so a consumer of these four reads the contract of the table owner and not the list read.
evidence: Lists header row 2 ('the rest are held and versioned in the Workbench. Each has one owner'); Lists rows with Source 'Workbench table rule_row', 'Workbench table document_type', 'Workbench table retention_rule' and 'Workbench table role'; Ownership Map sheet Tables rows rule_row P7, document_type P5, retention_rule P5 and role P4, with rulings ASM-A6-tables-3 and ASM-A6-tables-10; RWB-P3-E1043-CON section 12.7 (the three tables of the reference surface) and section 12.2 (the three consumed operations).
area: Data / where a source list is held after the split
proposed: Keep every list row and its Source cell unchanged, record the holding service in the new 'Owning service (D-RCV-60)' and 'Owning schema (D-RCV-60)' columns, and state in the route column which contract serves the list.

title: The Owner column is a stewardship role, not a service, and it is kept unchanged
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reference Data and Lists of Values v4.xlsx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
section: Lists column D; Reference tables column D
description: Every list and every reference-data row carries a business owner in column D, such as 'Center of excellence', 'Data steward and data product owner', 'Compliance' or 'Head of NPA'. None of those is one of the 19 services, and a business role does not say which schema holds the values. v5 keeps column D word for word and adds the owning service and the schema from the Ownership Map, so the two kinds of ownership sit side by side without either replacing the other.
evidence: Lists column D values (16 distinct role strings over 138 rows, for example 'Center of excellence' 78 times) and Reference tables column D; Ownership Map sheet Services (19 services) and sheet Tables (93 rows with an owner service and a schema); the Key sheet of v4 defines Codomain terms but no owner column.
area: Data / stewardship owner against service owner
owner_role: Data steward and data product owner
proposed: Read column D as the stewardship owner that approves a value, and the appended 'Owning service (D-RCV-60)' as the service that loads and serves it; the Key sheet gains the two terms that say so.

title: Five reference-data rows name no table, and no message table exists in the Ownership Map
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reference Data and Lists of Values v4.xlsx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
section: Reference tables rows 'Service levels and timers', 'Messages', 'Document types', 'Retention classes' and 'Masking rules'
description: The Table column of five of the 14 reference-data rows reads 'Reference table', so the row names no table and no owner. Four of them can be tied to a table by the Source cell of the matching list (document_type for LOV-DOC-TYPE, retention_rule for LOV-RETENTION, timer for the service levels, and masking_rule and reference_row by the Ownership Map). Messages has no table at all: the map carries 93 tables and none of them is a message or text catalogue, so the row is given reference_row in rwb_case as the versioned carrier of a message catalogue.
evidence: Reference tables sheet Table column rows 11, 13, 14, 15 and 16 ('Reference table', 'Reference table', 'Reference table', 'Reference table', 'Reference table'); Lists rows LOV-DOC-TYPE Source 'Workbench table document_type' and LOV-RETENTION Source 'Workbench table retention_rule'; Ownership Map sheet Tables rows timer P3, masking_rule P4, document_type P5, retention_rule P5, reference_row P3 and no message table among the 93 rows; Business Requirements Epic 1 RWB-E1-045 and the Error and Message Standard named in the 'Specified in' column.
area: Data / reference-data rows with no named table
proposed: Record the owner of each of the five rows from the map item behind it, name reference_row as the carrier of the message catalogue, and leave the Table cells of v4 unchanged; a named message table in a later Logical Data Model revision replaces the assumption.
